events.title: Elixir 0.1.0 released
events.summary: José Valim released Elixir v0.1.0 on March 2, 2011 — a Ruby-inspired language on the Erlang BEAM VM.
events.about: Elixir runs on Erlang's OTP with metaprogramming, pipelines (`|>`), and Phoenix for web. Powers Discord's real-time infrastructure, Pinterest backends, and IoT systems needing millions of connections. You get Erlang's fault tolerance with syntax closer to Ruby and modern tooling.

narrative.whyChosen: Elixir made the BEAM VM accessible to developers who found Erlang syntax daunting.
narrative.whyImportant: It revived interest in actor-model concurrency for web and real-time systems in the 2010s.
narrative.problemSolved: Erlang was proven for telecom but had a steep syntax curve; Valim wanted Ruby-like ergonomics on BEAM.
